text:
This five-minute analytics pitch is built like a professional sports investigation. It follows a clear storyline that separates raw numbers from real striker quality.



A sharp introduction to the research question.
A diagnosis of why total international goals is a limited ranking tool.
A deeper look at scoring ability, efficiency, and era context.

title: Who Is the Greatest International Striker of All Time?
text:
Question answered: Who really deserves the label “greatest international striker,” and why this is more than a goals leaderboard?
What data is shown: the dataset of every international goal, the leading scorers, and the metrics we will build from those records.
Best visualization: a short top-10 goals table plus a teaser statement that the raw leader is only the starting point.
Insight: The strongest case needs volume and context; raw totals are the first clue, not the final verdict.
The dataset records every international goal scored by an attacking player. In this investigation, we treat each goal as evidence and use it to test whether the all-time top names hold up once we measure quality, efficiency, and career profile.

Greatness is not only about a short peak. A long scoring career suggests durability and sustained quality.










The strongest candidates also score over many seasons.
Longevity strengthens the case because it shows sustained elite performance.

title: Who Is the Greatest International Striker of All Time?
text:
The best overall answer is the player who combines:

the highest scoring total,
the longest sustained career,
and the strongest open-play profile.

That combination offers the clearest evidence for being the greatest international striker of all time.

title: About
text:
This project is a sports analytics investigation that asks a focused question: who is the greatest international soccer striker of all time?


The dataset records every international goal by scorer, including:

match date,
national team,
scorer name,
goal minute,
penalty status,
goal type,
year and decade.

Each row is one goal, which means the analysis is built from the goals themselves rather than from match summaries.



The report evaluates the candidates with a professional lens:

raw scoring volume,
scoring quality through open-play share,
career consistency and efficiency,
era context,
a composite GOAT ranking model.




Greatest-striker discussions are common in soccer, but a strong analytic argument requires more than a leaderboard. This project emphasizes evidence, transparency, and the limits of the available data.



The current dataset does not include every context needed for a final historical judgement:

minutes played,
number of caps,
opponent strength,
match importance.

Those are valuable next steps for a deeper version of this project.

title: Who Is the Greatest International Striker of All Time?
text:
Limitations and next steps

The dataset does not include minutes played or caps, so efficiency is proxied by goals per active year.
We do not have full match importance or opponent strength for every goal.
Adding minutes, competition type, and match result would let us refine the model (and maybe change the pick).
